First vision walk surfaced a coherent lifestyle-bundle vision not previously documented in swarm-manager. Core architectural insight: inventory is the substrate that makes natural product suggestion work (without it, recommendations collapse to ads; with it, they become completion of a known need). Four new initiatives created: routines-app (authority-layer content for cleaning/inspection/maintenance/repair; closes the loop on physical chores), inventory-app (first-class substrate), contact-book-plus (revival of archived contact-book scenario), lifestyle-demand-validation (physical-guide market test runs parallel to routines-app engineering). Full vision frozen into each initiative's orchestration-summary.md. Type-B user framing, routines-as-resource-not-app principle, flexibility ladder (markdown -> list -> light DAG -> rich graph; BPMN 2.0 spec explicitly rejected), and long-horizon robot-orchestration arc are all preserved there. Monetization docs restructured to make consumer-products and affiliate-commerce first-class parallel revenue lines to subscription and services; both carry a mandatory recommendation-blindness architectural rule (agent producing a recommendation must not know what Vrooli sells or earns commission on — offer insertion is post-processing only).

Durable architectural principles landed in the 2026-04-23 walk (reference for future walks and agents): (1) Revenue optimization is a post-processing step, never an input to the recommendation layer. Applies to consumer-products and affiliate-commerce equally; codified in docs/monetization/revenue-lines/. (2) Inventory is the gating substrate for lifestyle-bundle consumer-product / affiliate activation — no scenario activates those revenue lines without inventory-aware state. (3) Routines are infrastructure, not a user-facing build-your-own-workflow product (the original Vrooli died partly from that trap). (4) Flexibility ladder for routines: markdown -> structured list -> light DAG -> rich graph; BPMN 2.0 as a spec is rejected. Vrooli-native rich graph carries the concepts (events / gateways / compensation / interrupt boundaries) without the spec weight. (5) Library and executor are distinct UX surfaces in the routines-app. (6) Prompt-manager distinction: team.enabled=true AND member heartbeats disabled is dormant not quiet. (7) Skills and docs must always invoke scenario CLIs, never raw API calls — if CLI lacks a command, add the command, do not work around. All seven belong in scenario READMEs and docs where applicable.

First calibration walk. Friction surfaced (each is a backlog item or fix): (1) Prep deliverable missing decision option keys — walker had to read decision docs separately to know A/B/C labels. (2) Prep conflates dormant teams (HBs disabled) with quiet teams (HBs active, nothing raised) — led to misdiagnosis of monetization and meta-optimization as active-but-quiet when all 5 + 6 member heartbeats were off. (3) Portfolio-manager is blind to in-flight platform work on branches — retrospective under-counted on a day with ~30 uncommitted swarm-manager files. Acceptable until Git Control Tower ships. (4) Skill referenced prompt-manager team decision-accept — CLI does not expose it; had to go to API PATCH directly. Root cause is a general CLI parity gap; filed as priority-5 backlog item. (5) Web Console TTS pronounces decision IDs inside code ticks as giant cardinal numbers (one quadrillion-plus); filed as TTS preprocessor fix. (6) Accepting a 'add edges' decision does not actually add the edges — only closes the governance step; manual edit follow-up required. Reasonable but non-obvious. (7) Decision phases + chore-audit + ideation ran long; future walks should cap decisions and reach the creative half faster. Positives: prep deliverable structure is strong — synthesized correctly, phase-by-phase; triage/creative split feels right; operator explicitly flagging dual-mode (do the walk + critique the walk) made friction surfacing much better. Operator confirmed morning-vision-walk does NOT need a permanent calibration mode — a few more walks converge steady state, then friction reports stop being novel.

TikTok signal: recurring complaints that incumbent inspector software (Spectora/HomeGauge/ISN) was acquired and inspection data is being resold to insurers, raising rates on homebuyers. OSS positioning ('you own the data, not us, not your insurer') is an unfakeable moat that SaaS structurally can't claim. Dual-audience candidate: pro inspectors (paid) + DIY homeowners (free OSS tier as credibility + word-of-mouth lead-gen). Order-dependent execution overlaps with routines-app substrate — likely vertical overlay rather than parallel scenario. Concerns: legal-compliance per region turns checklist into compliance product; liability framing must be explicit at product surface. Instinct: start with homeowner tier + OSS-credibility play; let pro discover; build compliance layer driven by actual jurisdictions. Open questions for next walk: folds into routines-app or sibling? data-sovereignty as wedge or one feature? pro-first or dual-from-start? Not initiative-ready — store and revisit if a second similar signal hits the same niche.

Operator surfaced regtech category — existing players (Vanta, Drata, Thomson Reuters Reg Intel, LexisNexis, Compliance.ai, Ascent). Architectural insight: competitive-intel and regulatory-intel are sibling scenarios on a hardened BAS substrate; vertical-compliance overlays (home-inspection, food-service, etc.) sit on top of regulatory-intel. Compound value: BAS hardening unlocks both intel scenarios; regulatory-intel unlocks N vertical overlays. Operator-confirmed positioning: (1) explicit no-legal-responsibility framing at product surface, not buried in TOS; (2) priced accordingly — not Vanta/TR-tier prices that imply liability we don't take; (3) operator-supplied data sources are first-class — users plug in their own paywalled subscriptions/custom feeds. Concerns: supersession/staleness detection harder than ingestion. Open questions (left open per operator): (a) one scenario with vertical configs vs thin substrate + separate vertical scenarios (instinct: latter); (b) first vertical — inspection / food-service / Vanta-clone; (c) detailed pricing/liability frame. Existing accessibility-compliance-hub scenario covers a11y only. Not initiative-ready.

Friction inventory from 2026-04-25 walk (third instance of morning-vision-walk skill, intentionally framed as process-friction analysis):

#0 last-handoff.md doesn't record consumption — second walk same day re-reads same file as if fresh.
#1 Walk-timing/prep-staleness — skill assumes morning; prep regenerates only at 5 AM; no on-demand prep refresh; no late-walk branch. Today's walk ran at 19:00 against 14h-old prep.
#2 Phase 1 has no overflow guardrail — operator's open floor today covered ~5 future-action items + one strategic question, colliding with later phases. Skill should cap open-floor scope; capture overflow into Phase 8 queue.
#3 Prep didn't ask the upstream strategic question of whether web-console-readiness is the right headliner — it reported the initiative as 'now exists at 0/N' as a fact rather than surfacing the headliner-fit question. Prep should run a 'has-recent-acceptance produced the right downstream-question' check.
#4 +3 net portfolio attribution gap — prep agent reports count delta but lacks per-initiative created_at filter to attribute net-new initiatives precisely. Small data gap; the prep agent itself flagged this.
#5 capability-gap decisions are accept/reject-shaped but the right operator response is almost always 'investigate and file delta items.' Mismatch between decision-shape and work-shape; either the decision schema needs a 'scope-hint' state or capability-gap should not be a decision.
#6 market-validator pricing-trough decision filed at wrong abstraction — agent didn't check Stripe (source of truth) and concluded 'pricing undecided' when reality is 'pricing decided in Stripe but undocumented in PRICING.md.' Member agents need read-access to operator-controlled sources of truth before filing decisions that depend on them.
#7 Operator wasn't aware that docs/marketing/strategy/STRATEGY.md voice canon already exists. Prep agent surfaced two publish-proposals without linking the canon or showing whether contrarian had scored them against it. Pre-decision context should reference the relevant canon + show its application status.
#8 Proposal-vs-actual-state sync loose — team-agent-optimizer filed dec-...818847 for a fix the operator had already shipped to run-introspector. Member agents need a way to verify 'is this still relevant' before re-proposing.
#9 Skill assumes single-walk-per-day; no protocol for late or repeat walks. Subset of #1 but worth its own entry.
#10 Prep snapshot vs live queue drift — by Phase 8, the toolchain queue had already re-shaped (dec-...430656 was superseded mid-day by dec-...516340 with new 36-violation/1-Critical baseline). Skill should re-pull pending decisions at walk-time before executing accepts, not trust prep snapshot alone.
#11 Capability-gap routing in prep doc didn't match actual queue location — competitive-intel was reported as 'on meta-optimization' but actually lived on marketing-crew (its originating team). First decision-accept attempt failed because of this. Prep doc should include exact (team, decision-id) tuples, not narrative routing.

Most leveraged fixes: #1+#9+#10 (re-runnable / live-queue-aware prep), #5 (decision schema for scope-hint capability-gaps), #11 (precise routing in prep), #7 (canon awareness in prep).

Captured at vision walk #4 (2026-04-27) chore-audit phase. Generative research method for seeding family-bundle scenario candidates and identifying capability gaps in the Vrooli platform.

METHOD: Monitor popular homelab apps and self-hosted-software communities (e.g., r/selfhosted, awesome-selfhosted lists, homelab-focused YouTube channels, X posts about homelab setups) for what people are running locally, what they're using each app for, and what gaps they report. Each popular homelab app becomes a candidate scenario for the family bundle. Each gap reported becomes a candidate capability for Vrooli.

SOURCE BOOKMARK that surfaced this method: viral X post about someone using Claude Code (Anthropic's coding agent) to set up a personal homelab containing multiple self-hosted services. The post both validated the audience (people who want local-first software) and listed specific apps the person built — those apps are direct family-bundle scenario candidates.

EXAMPLES of homelab apps that map to family-bundle scenario candidates (non-exhaustive seed list):
- Media server (Plex / Jellyfin / Emby) — capture as low-priority swarm-manager idea
- Home automation hub (Home Assistant) — already valuable as substrate; possibly an existing initiative
- Password / secrets manager (Bitwarden / Vaultwarden) — overlaps with planned Vault resource integration
- Photo management (Immich / PhotoPrism)
- File sync / cloud replacement (Nextcloud / Syncthing)
- DNS / ad blocking (Pi-hole / AdGuard Home)
- Network monitoring / dashboards (Uptime Kuma)
- Recipe management (Mealie / Tandoor) — overlaps with existing recipe-book scenario
- Bookmark management / read-it-later (Wallabag / Linkwarden) — overlaps with the BIH rework initiative

WHEN TO RUN THIS RESEARCH METHOD:
- During family-bundle planning sessions — to identify scenario candidates and prioritize
- When the BIH ideation-extraction agent (per initiative bookmark-intelligence-hub-rework-and-ideation) is active — homelab-app bookmarks naturally surface scenario-candidate classifications
- Periodically (suggest: quarterly) as a director-swarm research item to refresh the candidate list

OWNER: This is a research method, not an automated agent loop. It informs initiative-proposal decisions and family-bundle scenario prioritization. Researcher (marketing-crew) could partially automate the audience-scanning portion once BAS or formal API capability matures.

Process-feedback from vision walk #4 (2026-04-27). Captured at Phase 9 wrap-up. Frictions and observations to inform next walks and the prep agent.

CUMULATIVE FRICTION TALLY (from this walk):

1. WALKS ARE SKIP-TOLERANT. Operator skipped 2026-04-26 walk intentionally to test what happens. System stayed coherent — pending decisions persisted, prep deliverable picked up cleanly, no team-state divergence. Validates the walk as workload-flexible, not strictly daily. Captured as durable feedback memory feedback_vision_walk_artifact_review.md.

2. PREP ENUMERATES *WHAT* BUT MISSES *STRATEGIC SHAPE*. The 24h sandbox/agent-manager/lifecycle work was described as platform machinery in prep, but the real shape was upstream-unblock-for-review-confidence-and-GCT-integration. The why is what makes the walk decide accurately. Suggested prep enhancement: when summarizing a categorys completions, attempt to identify the strategic frame (eg unblock for X, prerequisite for Y, throughput for Z) rather than only categorizing tactically.

3. MAJOR ARCHITECTURAL PRINCIPLES NEED REPO HOMES. Operator articulated wrap-not-use mid-walk; nothing in the repo encoded it. Future agents would reconstruct from practice. Partially addressed during Phase 8 today: wrap-not-use is now documented in docs/concepts/ARCHITECTURE.md (Core Architectural Principles section) and referenced from AGENTS.md. Pattern to watch: when an operator articulates a load-bearing principle that does not yet have a docs home, surface that as an immediate follow-up (file as backlog or seed-now) rather than letting it stay verbal.

4. PREP TREATS CAPABILITY-GAPS AS TRANSIENT OUTAGES. dec-1777232213798487055 was framed in prep as agent-manager-is-back-mark-resolved — but the rationale claimed silent-crash-on-idle as a behavior pattern. Prep collapsed two different claims (current symptom vs root pattern). Suggested prep enhancement: when summarizing capability-gap recommendations, distinguish symptom-resolution from root-claim-resolution.

5. CLI HELP-TEXT DRIFT (decision-accept). Help said --selected required; actual error message reveals it should distinguish multi-option vs single-proposal. Fixed during Phase 8 today (teams.go:746 + 3058). Pattern: CLI help text and error messages should be co-derived; drift between them is a tooling signal worth fixing immediately when noticed.

6. FINANCIAL-TRACKER QUIET-SNAPSHOT EATS WALK ATTENTION. 8+ days of identical no-change-since-2026-04-24 with operator-inputs.json still null on 7 fields. Operator declared no-op today. Continuing-as-is is the worst path; operator should populate or mute, but neither has happened. Pattern: long-running quiet-snapshot artifacts should auto-suppress in prep when their content has not materially changed across N consecutive snapshots.

7. PREP CHAR-COUNTS DIVERGED FROM ARTIFACT. Prep listed 197/184/225/232/184/174 for the dev-log thread; actual draft was 210/204/228/233/166/200. Transcription drift in artifact metadata. Suggested prep enhancement: pull artifact metadata from authoritative source (campaign-drafts.jsonl entry has char_counts field) rather than recomputing.

8. DRAFT-BEARING DECISIONS NEED ARTIFACT IN PREP. Captured as durable feedback memory feedback_vision_walk_artifact_review.md. Short artifacts (tweets, thread, ≤500 words) should be read aloud in walk; long artifacts get a markdown path the operator can open in their console. Operator should never approve copy sight-unseen.

PROCESS-MECHANICS OBSERVATIONS FROM TODAY:

9. MULTIPLE DIVERGENCES IN ONE WALK WORKS WELL. Walk #4 had 3 explicit divergences (dev-log content strategy, project-level documentation gap, BIH rework + bookmark capture). Skill supports this naturally via repeated checkpoint sections. Each divergence stayed bounded by its own acceptance criterion; resume-on-completion was clean each time. Pattern: do not artificially limit divergences — they are how high-density walks deliver actual structural change.

10. PROPOSE-SCOPE-THEN-EXECUTE PATTERN IS EFFECTIVE FOR DIVERGENCES. Each divergence today followed: (a) propose explicit acceptance criterion + scope, (b) get operator sign-off, (c) execute with task tracking. This pattern kept context-coherence high and prevented scope creep. Worth preserving as the divergence default.

11. THIRD DIVERGENCE WITH PARTIAL EXECUTION + PARTIAL CAPTURE WORKED. The BIH divergence simultaneously created an initiative for the work AND captured peripheral items in their right homes (notebook, knowledge entries, revenue lines, capability-flags doc). Different artifacts in different homes per their nature, all coordinated under one acceptance criterion. Pattern: divergences can plan-and-execute multiple parallel structural moves so long as each artifact has a single owner and clear placement decision.

12. PHASE-8 FORMALIZATION CAPTURED THE LOOSE CANDIDATES THAT WOULD HAVE EVAPORATED. 5 loose candidates accumulated across divergences; Phase 8 sorted them into 2-do-now / 2-file / 1-skip. Pattern: even a divergence-heavy walk should still run Phase 8 — divergences capture their own immediate work, but cross-cutting candidates emerge from the conversation and need explicit triage.
